headline: Govt says no better alternative to fuel price hike despite public suffering
summary: Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman stated that the decision was necessary and not imposed by the IMF, despite the potential for increased hardship for ordinary citizens.
details: The government has defended its decision to raise fuel prices, stating there was no other viable alternative despite the expected increase in suffering for ordinary people.
Zahed Ur Rahman, adviser to the prime minister on information and broadcasting, acknowledged that the hike would cause hardship but argued it was a necessary step.
He emphasized that no government would deliberately take such an unpopular decision shortly before local government elections, suggesting the move was unavoidable.
The adviser clarified that the fuel price increase was not a condition imposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Beyond fuel prices, Zahed addressed the political climate, stating the government sees no political crisis despite opposition movements and protests in Dhaka.
He noted that incidents like crude bomb explosions and buses being set on fire would not create a political crisis for the democratically elected government.

Regarding the opposition's demands, he compared current movements to political protests in India, suggesting that pressure should be focused on specific failures rather than demanding government resignation.
Zahed also mentioned that an agreement to purchase Boeing aircraft might be place during the prime minister's upcoming visit to the United States, as the decision to buy had been made previously.
caption:
The government admits the fuel price hike will increase public suffering but claims there was "no better alternative."

The government has defended its decision to raise fuel prices, stating there was no other viable alternative despite the expected increase in suffering for ordinary people.

He emphasized that no government would deliberately take such an unpopular decision shortly before local government elections, suggesting the move was unavoidable.

The adviser clarified that the fuel price increase was not a condition imposed by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

Beyond fuel prices, Zahed addressed the political climate, stating the government sees no political crisis despite opposition movements and protests in Dhaka.

He noted that incidents like crude bomb explosions and buses being set on fire would not create a political crisis for the democratically elected government.

Regarding the opposition's demands, he compared current movements to political protests in India, suggesting that pressure should be focused on specific failures rather than demanding government resignation.

Zahed also mentioned that an agreement to purchase Boeing aircraft might be place during the prime minister's upcoming visit to the United States, as the decision to buy had been made previously.

headline: Ex-MP Mahfuzur Rahman arrested in Gulshan
summary: The former lawmaker from Sandwip constituency was detained by the DB police from a house in the capital.
details: The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has detained former Member of Parliament Mahfuzur Rahman.
He was picked up from a residence in Gulshan, Dhaka, during a raid conducted around 2:00 AM on Monday night based on secret information.
A.F.M. Anwar Hossain Khan, Deputy Commissioner of the DB Gulshan division, confirmed the detention on Tuesday.
The former lawmaker, who represented the Sandwip constituency (Chattogram-3), was reportedly hiding in the house at the time of the operation.
Police officials stated that he may be arrested in connection with a case involving a flash procession and cocktail explosions in Mohakhali.
caption:
Former Sandwip MP Mahfuzur Rahman has been detained by DB police from a house in Gulshan.

The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has detained former Member of Parliament Mahfuzur Rahman.

He was picked up from a residence in Gulshan, Dhaka, during a raid conducted around 2:00 AM on Monday night based on secret information.

A.F.M. Anwar Hossain Khan, Deputy Commissioner of the DB Gulshan division, confirmed the detention on Tuesday.

The former lawmaker, who represented the Sandwip constituency (Chattogram-3), was reportedly hiding in the house at the time of the operation.

Police officials stated that he may be arrested in connection with a case involving a flash procession and cocktail explosions in Mohakhali.
